run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:54:48Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy error signal is real and is made of HTTP 504 gateway-timeout spans from the proxy's own ingress spans, not of proxy restarts: the proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm has been running since 09:42:49Z with 0 restarts and its Deployment is 1/1 ready. A full trace shows the mechanism: the load generator's POST got a 504 after 15.0 s because frontend's POST /api/checkout stayed open ~93 s inside checkout's 'orders publish' span, which ended in ERROR 'circuit breaker is open'; checkout pod logs independently show 'kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' and 'read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout'. Chaos-mesh events show a Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh) spawning NetworkChaos objects every minute from 10:14:17Z to 10:22:17Z that explicitly applied chaos to otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l and both kafka pods, each recovered ~55 s later. That partition is the best-supported origin of the Kafka produce failures behind the 504s for the 10:14-10:22 escalation, but the same 504/produce failure is already present in the first available metric samples (~09:55-10:00), i.e. before the earliest visible chaos application, so the onset of the alert at 09:54:48Z is not fully explained. A second, independent error component hit frontend-proxy from 10:14 to 10:26: frontend's client spans to AdService/GetAds failed (0.05/s rising to 0.77/s) and frontend returned errors on /api/data, while the ad service recorded no GetAds spans at all between 10:18 and 10:22 and frontend's tcp.connect spans errored; the ad pod ad-554b849958-4chjq was OOMKilled (exit 137) and its container restarted at 10:12:29Z. That restart is observed, but a causal link to the AdService failures is unverified because no traces after 10:12:22Z and no ad/frontend logs before ~10:22Z were retrievable. A kafka-internal KRaft signal (repeated StaleBrokerEpochException 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' and failing assignReplicasToDirs on broker 1) is a further candidate for the prolonged produce failures and is reported as a hypothesis. All flagd fault-injection flags were 'off' in flagd-config, so feature-flag fault injection is not supported as the cause.

claims.text: frontend-proxy carried nonzero span errors from the first available sample: STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0.206/s at 09:56Z, 0.558/s at 09:59Z, then a steady ~0.33-0.51/s through 10:14Z, rising to 1.02/s at 10:15Z, 1.69/s at 10:17Z and a peak 1.97/s at 10:18Z, then 1.86-1.97/s to 10:21Z, 1.31/s at 10:23Z, 0.64/s at 10:25Z, 0.43/s at 10:27Z and 0.13/s at 10:29Z, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans stayed roughly 15-18/s.

The frontend-proxy error spans are on the 'ingress' span before 10:15Z (ERROR 0.32-0.56/s, egress ERROR exactly 0), and from 10:15Z both 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' error (ingress 1.19/s, egress 0.75/s at 10:19Z).

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans are 'ingress' spans with error=true, http.status_code=504 and otel.status_code=ERROR at ~15,000,000 us duration, each with a child 'router frontend egress' span carrying error=true and http.status_code=0 at ~15,000,000 us.

Trace 2438a213601165c62df043bfa2e22ed5 (started 10:10:30Z) shows the 504 chain: load-generator 'user_checkout_multi' 15.4 s, load-generator POST 504 ERROR 15.0 s, frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 ERROR 15.0 s with child 'router frontend egress' error http.status_code 0, frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 93.0 s ending http.status_code 200, frontend client 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 92.6 s, checkout server 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 92.0 s, and checkout 'orders publish' 91.9 s ending ERROR with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l logs record 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open' and 'kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' at 10:22:15Z, then 'client/metadata got error from broker 1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout' and 'Closed connection to broker kafka:9092' at 10:22:56Z.

Chaos-mesh events show a Schedule named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh spawning NetworkChaos objects otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-fkbbr (10:14:17Z), -96js2 (10:15:17Z), -c88bd (10:16:17Z), -tfpsw (10:17:17Z), -t2rzv (10:18:17Z), -fnppk (10:19:17Z), -znv8m (10:20:17Z), -j8wrs (10:21:17Z) and -dtwx (10:22:17Z); each reports 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l' plus otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-xclnk and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-skk8d, then 'Time up according to the duration' about 55 s later and 'Recovered' for the same pods, with matching PodNetworkChaos updates in namespace otel-demo.

A second error component appears from 10:14Z to 10:26Z: frontend client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' ERROR rate 0.048/s at 10:14Z, 0.279/s at 10:15Z, 0.641/s at 10:17Z, 0.767/s at 10:18Z, 0.537/s at 10:22Z, 0.356/s at 10:23Z and 0 at 10:26Z; frontend 'GET', 'GET /api/data' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' show the identical error rate, and frontend 'tcp.connect' ERROR rate is 0.026-0.041/s over 10:14-10:20Z.

The ad service's own spans stop during that window: 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' rate 0.70/s at 10:01-10:14Z, 0.45/s at 10:15Z, 0.25/s at 10:16Z, 0.07/s at 10:17Z, 0 at 10:18-10:22Z, then 0.38/s at 10:23Z; 'getAdsByCategory' and 'getRandomAds' likewise fall to 0 for 10:18-10:22Z; the ad service's only error spans in the window are 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' ERROR 0.168/s, 0.142/s, 0.138/s and 0.122/s at 10:23-10:26Z.

Pod ad-554b849958-4chjq has restartCount 1, its last container state is terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at finishedAt 2026-11-17T10:12:29Z, and the current container started at 10:12:29Z with Ready True from 10:12:30Z; its 'ad' container limits are cpu 50m / memory 450Mi with requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

The only Pod-kind events recorded in namespace otel-demo during 09:59:44-10:22:43Z are for ad-554b849958-4chjq: Pulled, Created and Started at 10:12:29Z, consistent with the single ad container restart.

The flagd-config ConfigMap key demo.flagd.json defines adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, and every one has defaultVariant 'off'.

All otel-demo Deployments report available=ready=spec replicas (ad 1/1, checkout 1/1, frontend 1/1, frontend-proxy 1/1, kafka 2/2), and in the pod inventory every otel-demo pod except ad has restartCount 0, including checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l, kafka-ff7884766-xclnk, kafka-ff7884766-skk8d and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm (created 09:42:49Z).

Kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-xclnk (broker nodeId=1) logs between 10:22:13Z and 10:23:18Z repeatedly show '[QuorumController id=1] assignReplicasToDirs: event failed with StaleBrokerEpochException ... Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' roughly every 10 s and a CreateTopics result of TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS for topic 'orders', plus continuous __cluster_metadata-0 segment rolling/deletion.

checkout's error span rate is essentially flat across the whole observed period at 0.29/s (10:00Z), 0.42/s (10:05Z), 0.48/s (10:10Z), 0.41/s (10:15Z), 0.46/s (10:20Z), 0.45/s (10:25Z) and 0.22/s (10:30Z), i.e. checkout was already erroring at the same level before the first visible NetworkChaos application at 10:14:17Z.

Service endpoints exist and have no not-ready addresses for the relevant services at query time: ad 100.96.4.91:8080, checkout 100.96.1.134:8080, frontend 100.96.3.21:8080, kafka 100.96.2.21 and 100.96.4.61 on ports 9092 and 9093.

Most likely origin of the 504 timeouts: the NetworkChaos objects spawned by Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition (chaos-mesh) partitioned checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l from both kafka pods, so checkout's Kafka produce blocked ~92 s (error 'circuit breaker is open', metadata read 'i/o timeout' to kafka:9092), frontend's /api/checkout exceeded the proxy's 15 s timeout, and frontend-proxy emitted ingress 504 errors; the 10:14-10:22Z applications coincide with the largest error increase and the recovery of the error rate by 10:27-10:29Z. It does not by itself explain the identical 504/produce failures already present before 10:14:17Z.

The 10:14-10:26Z error increase on frontend-proxy (ingress and egress) was driven by frontend's /api/data failures to AdService/GetAds after the ad container was OOMKilled and restarted at 10:12:29Z; ad served no GetAds spans at all between 10:18Z and 10:22Z while frontend's client GetAds spans and tcp.connect spans errored, then ad traffic resumed from ~10:23Z. This link is unverified: no trace data exists after ~10:12:22Z and no ad or frontend logs before ~10:22Z were retrievable.

Kafka's own KRaft state may be an independent contributor to the prolonged 'orders' produce failures: broker nodeId=1 reports repeated StaleBrokerEpochException 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' with failing assignReplicasToDirs against its own QuorumController, which is consistent with partitions not being properly assigned on that broker (checkout also saw 'Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker'). No evidence ties these log lines to a specific failed produce, and kafka logs are only readable from 10:22:13Z.

The alert's stated start 09:54:48Z may mark the onset of trace-metric availability rather than a new fault: the first frontend-proxy error sample in the metric is at 09:56Z and the 10-minute checkout error rate first returns a point at 10:00Z with an already-elevated 0.29/s, so errors of the same shape appear to predate all observable telemetry.

Feature-flag fault injection is not supported as the cause of this error rate: the demo.flagd.json in ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo has every fault flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) at defaultVariant 'off'.

A frontend-proxy restart, crash or resource failure is not the source of its error rate: pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm was created 09:42:49Z with restartCount 0 and the frontend-proxy Deployment is 1/1 available/ready, while the error spans are downstream-timeout 504s with 15 s duration.

checkout and both kafka pods show no container restarts and their Deployments are fully available (checkout 1/1, kafka 2/2), so the Kafka produce failures are not explained by a pod crash or rollout of those workloads.

Retrieve and review the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition and its NetworkChaos specs (selector, direction, target, duration) and its creation time, to establish whether the checkout-to-kafka partition was already active before the first retained chaos event at 10:14:17Z and thus explains the alert onset at 09:54:48Z.

Investigate the ad container's OOMKill and slow post-restart availability: verify why a container limited to 450Mi and 50m CPU was OOMKilled at 10:12:29Z and why the ad service registered no GetAds spans until ~10:22Z despite reporting Ready from 10:12:30Z.

Have the Kafka owner check broker nodeId=1's KRaft registration/epoch state (StaleBrokerEpochException 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10', failing assignReplicasToDirs) and the leader/partition assignment of topic 'orders', since that can independently make produces fail.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so when the chaos Schedule/NetworkChaos, the ad workload and any configuration were created or changed cannot be verified.

Prometheus returned no data for an alerting rule named RequestErrorRate (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing), so the exact alert expression, threshold and unit of the annotation's 'current: 1.5999999999999999' could not be verified.

Jaeger trace coverage in this dataset ends around 2026-11-17T10:12:22Z: traces_search for frontend-proxy over 10:14-10:20Z returned nothing, so the 10:14-10:33Z error paths (including the AdService/GetAds failures) have no span-level evidence.

Application logs before ~10:22Z were not retrievable: frontend-675fd7b5c5-djtdf returned zero log lines both with and without an error filter, and ad/checkout/kafka logs were only readable from ~10:22:13-10:22:31Z onward, so the 09:54-10:22Z application-level history is unknown.

NetworkChaos and Schedule are chaos-mesh custom resources not covered by the permitted Kubernetes kinds, so their specs (selector, direction, delay/loss, duration) and their existence before 10:14:17Z could not be read; only events emitted for them are evidence.

The cause of the identical checkout 'orders publish' failures and frontend-proxy 504s present in the first available metric samples (~09:55-10:00Z, before the first visible NetworkChaos application at 10:14:17Z) is not established; both an earlier instance of the same network partition and kafka-internal state remain unverified.

Kafka server-side span metrics are missing: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="kafka"} returned no series in 09:56-10:33Z, and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count had no service_name label values in the window, so neither Kafka nor gRPC-level error rates could be measured.

Whether the frontend-proxy error spans in 10:15-10:26Z carry HTTP 500 (as opposed to 504) could not be confirmed because no traces exist for that interval; the frontend /api/data error spans were observed only through metrics.
The ad Pod's previous container logs are not available (the log tool reported 'previous terminated container "ad" ... not found'), so the OOM reason itself could not be read.
next_steps: Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition and its NetworkChaos objects (spec, target pods, direction, duration, creationTimestamp) and correlate their active intervals with the error-rate timeline.
Query change history / audit logs for chaos-mesh and otel-demo to determine what changed between 09:42Z (namespace pods created) and 09:54:48Z (alert start).
If Jaeger retention allows, re-query traces for the 10:14-10:30Z window to capture the AdService/GetAds failure spans and their status descriptions.
Obtain frontend pod logs for 10:00-10:30Z from the log backend or node, since the frontend container's stdout was not returned by the log tool.
Review the ad container's memory limit (450Mi) against its usage and its post-restart startup path, and consider whether the 50m CPU limit delays recovery.
Ask the Kafka owner to validate broker nodeId=1's epoch registration and the 'orders' topic partition assignment/leadership during 09:42-10:30Z.

hypothesis.text: Most likely origin of the 504 timeouts: the NetworkChaos objects spawned by Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition (chaos-mesh) partitioned checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l from both kafka pods, so checkout's Kafka produce blocked ~92 s (error 'circuit breaker is open', metadata read 'i/o timeout' to kafka:9092), frontend's /api/checkout exceeded the proxy's 15 s timeout, and frontend-proxy emitted ingress 504 errors; the 10:14-10:22Z applications coincide with the largest error increase and the recovery of the error rate by 10:27-10:29Z. It does not by itself explain the identical 504/produce failures already present before 10:14:17Z.

The 10:14-10:26Z error increase on frontend-proxy (ingress and egress) was driven by frontend's /api/data failures to AdService/GetAds after the ad container was OOMKilled and restarted at 10:12:29Z; ad served no GetAds spans at all between 10:18Z and 10:22Z while frontend's client GetAds spans and tcp.connect spans errored, then ad traffic resumed from ~10:23Z. This link is unverified: no trace data exists after ~10:12:22Z and no ad or frontend logs before ~10:22Z were retrievable.

Kafka's own KRaft state may be an independent contributor to the prolonged 'orders' produce failures: broker nodeId=1 reports repeated StaleBrokerEpochException 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' with failing assignReplicasToDirs against its own QuorumController, which is consistent with partitions not being properly assigned on that broker (checkout also saw 'Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker'). No evidence ties these log lines to a specific failed produce, and kafka logs are only readable from 10:22:13Z.

The alert's stated start 09:54:48Z may mark the onset of trace-metric availability rather than a new fault: the first frontend-proxy error sample in the metric is at 09:56Z and the 10-minute checkout error rate first returns a point at 10:00Z with an already-elevated 0.29/s, so errors of the same shape appear to predate all observable telemetry.

recommendation.text: Retrieve and review the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition and its NetworkChaos specs (selector, direction, target, duration) and its creation time, to establish whether the checkout-to-kafka partition was already active before the first retained chaos event at 10:14:17Z and thus explains the alert onset at 09:54:48Z.

Investigate the ad container's OOMKill and slow post-restart availability: verify why a container limited to 450Mi and 50m CPU was OOMKilled at 10:12:29Z and why the ad service registered no GetAds spans until ~10:22Z despite reporting Ready from 10:12:30Z.

Have the Kafka owner check broker nodeId=1's KRaft registration/epoch state (StaleBrokerEpochException 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10', failing assignReplicasToDirs) and the leader/partition assignment of topic 'orders', since that can independently make produces fail.

counter_evidence.text: checkout and both kafka pods show no container restarts and their Deployments are fully available (checkout 1/1, kafka 2/2), so the Kafka produce failures are not explained by a pod crash or rollout of those workloads.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Feature-flag fault injection is not supported as the cause of this error rate: the demo.flagd.json in ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo has every fault flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) at defaultVariant 'off'.
